1. Executive Summary

This report documents the empirical results of testing volume-surge indicators constructed from COMEX gold futures volume as predictors of short-horizon forward returns in the SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) during the US cash close session (15:00–16:00 ET). The evaluation covers completed Sections A through D using the one-axis-at-a-time methodology implemented in lup-2a.ipynb and lup-2b.ipynb.

  • Baseline Signal (GC_30): The baseline specification (GC total volume divided by its trailing 30-minute rolling mean, divided by an expanding mean of past absolute raw values) produced Pearson IC values of −0.003982 at 1m, +0.000964 at 5m, +0.004750 at 10m, and +0.016617 (Spearman −0.000850) at 30m ($n=14,609$). A continuous diagnostic ($S_t \times R_{t,t+30}$) produced an average return of +0.5937 bps per observation and an annualized Sharpe of 0.700.
  • Lookback Length (Section A.1): In Section A.1, the 90-bar lookback (A1_lb90_h30) produced a 30-minute Pearson IC of +0.029585 (Spearman +0.014699, Sharpe 0.992, avg return +0.820 bps), and the 120-bar lookback (A1_lb120_h30) produced +0.028562 (Spearman +0.018539, Sharpe 0.933), compared with +0.016617 for the 30-bar baseline.
  • Normalization, Central Tendency, and Transformations (Sections A.2, B.1–B.3): Rolling-1950 normalization produced a 30m Pearson IC of +0.017248, while rolling-60 produced +0.007401. A median denominator produced +0.017526. Percentile rank scaling produced +0.017110. A logarithmic ratio produced a 30m Pearson IC of +0.012727, compared with +0.016617 for the linear baseline.
  • Total-Volume, Uptick-Volume, and Downtick-Volume Surges (Section B.4): At the 1-minute horizon, uptick-volume surge produced a Pearson IC of +0.035301 (Spearman +0.100261, Sharpe 3.059), downtick-volume surge produced −0.020735, and total-volume surge produced −0.003982. At 30m, uptick-volume surge was +0.015666 and total-volume surge was +0.016617. The 1m uptick-volume surge result is retained on a provisional basis pending burst-level de-duplication testing to address potential same-burst dependence.
  • Instrument Sets (Section B.5): Standalone COMEX GC volume produced a 30m Pearson IC of +0.016617. Micro Gold (MGC) produced +0.014011, an ounce-weighted GC+MGC composite produced +0.016358, and an equity ETF volume basket produced +0.013819.
  • Static vs. Dynamic Surge (Section C.1): Continuous velocity and acceleration constructions produced Pearson IC values ranging between −0.0166 and +0.0012 across tested horizons, not improving on the static baseline (30m IC +0.016617).
  • Confirmation Duration & Burst Phases (Sections C.2 & C.3): In event-conditioned screens, a 4-bar confirmation rule ($N=4$) produced a mean 30-minute forward return of +3.937 bps ($n=129$ events; 115 non-overlapping trades), compared with +0.620 bps for $N=1$. Conditioned on an elevated surge state, the rising flank phase produced a mean 30m return of +1.760 bps ($n=569$) and persistence produced +1.678 bps ($n=1,173$), compared with +0.620 bps at onset ($n=1,994$).
  • Time-of-Day Windows (Section D): In the early-close window (15:00–15:30 ET), the 30-minute Pearson IC was +0.028412 ($n=7,328$), compared with +0.001267 in the late-close window (15:30–16:00 ET, $n=7,281$) and +0.016617 across the full close ($n=14,609$).

These results document the completed single-axis screening through Section D. Section E, joint survivor testing, and out-of-sample testing remain uncompleted.

2. Research Objective & Scope Boundaries

The research objective is to test whether short bursts of trading activity in gold futures predict short-horizon GLD returns, and to determine which definition of a volume surge provides the strongest predictive relationship.

The evaluation adheres to a strict one-axis-at-a-time design:

$$\text{Subsection Specification} = \text{Baseline Specification} + \Delta(\text{Tested Dimension Only})$$

The one-axis design changes only the dimension under study while holding the remaining baseline specification fixed, allowing the effect of that design choice on the screening results to be compared cleanly. Settings evaluated in other subsections are not combined into the current search grid.

Volume Surge vs. Directional Trade Metrics
A total volume surge measures activity intensity relative to a trailing reference, not price momentum. The baseline indicator is constructed purely from total volume turnover. In Section B.4, uptick-volume surge scales uptick volume against its own trailing uptick baseline; it is not a net difference or ratio between uptick and downtick volumes.

3. Data and Instrument Construction

The analysis is implemented on 1-minute bar data from August 17, 2025 to August 21, 2026, comprising 246 active trading days.

1. COMEX Futures Construction

The futures dataset (comex_60.csv) contains 1-minute bars with fields: Time, symbol, vwap_traded_volume, uptick_volume, and downtick_volume. The symbol root is designated as MGC if the symbol begins with "MGC", and GC otherwise. For each minute bar, volume, uptick volume, and downtick volume are aggregated across all trading expiries by grouping by Time and root.

2. Equity ETF Target Construction

The equity dataset (equity_60.csv) contains 1-minute bars for GLD, GLDM, IAU, and IAUM. The primary target price $P_t$ is the GLD volume-weighted average price (vwap).

3. Forward Return Clock-Time Mapping

Forward returns are computed using exact clock-time lookup across horizons $h \in \{1, 5, 10, 30\}$ minutes:

$$R_{t, t+h}^{\text{GLD}} = \frac{P_{t+h}^{\text{GLD}}}{P_t^{\text{GLD}}} - 1$$

If the exact future timestamp required for a horizon is unavailable, that observation is unavailable for that horizon.

4. Observation Window

The baseline close-session window is $15:00 \le t < 16:00$ Eastern Time. After dropping observations where either the signal or the forward target is unavailable, the baseline 30-minute forward return screen contains 14,609 paired observations across 246 trading days.

4. Quantitative Methodology & Diagnostic Framework

Continuous Signal Diagnostic Convention

For continuous indicators, strategy returns are computed as:

$$\text{strategy\_return}_t = S_t \cdot R_{t, t+h}^{\text{GLD}}$$

No entry threshold is applied in continuous diagnostics, and continuous signals are not converted into binary long-only rules. The reported metrics are:

  • Signed Pearson IC: $\text{Corr}(S_t, R_{t,t+h}^{\text{GLD}})$. Primary ranking metric for continuous screens. Absolute IC is not used for ranking.
  • Spearman Rank IC: Secondary diagnostic and tiebreaker.
  • Avg bps: Mean strategy return in basis points: $\text{mean}(S_t \cdot R_{t,t+h}^{\text{GLD}} \times 10,000)$.
  • Hit Rate: Proportion of observations where strategy return is positive: $\text{mean}(S_t \cdot R_{t,t+h}^{\text{GLD}} > 0)$.
  • Annualized Sharpe: Computed on daily aggregated strategy returns: $(\text{mean}_{\text{daily}} / \text{std}_{\text{daily}}) \times \sqrt{252}$.
  • Annualized Sortino: $(\text{mean}_{\text{daily}} / \text{downside\_std}_{\text{daily}}) \times \sqrt{252}$, where downside std is computed on negative daily returns ($ddof=1$).
  • n_obs & n_days: Total valid minute observations and distinct trading days.

Event-Based Diagnostic Convention (Sections C.2 & C.3)

Sections C.2 and C.3 evaluate discrete burst states rather than continuous variables. For event screens, reported metrics are:

  • Mean Forward bps: Event-conditioned mean return: $\mathbb{E}[R_{t, t+h}^{\text{GLD}} \times 10,000 \mid E_t = 1]$. Primary ranking metric for C.2/C.3.
  • Hit Rate: Proportion of events with positive forward return.
  • Event Count ($n$): Number of qualifying event bars.
  • Non-Overlapping Trade Diagnostics (C.2): Positions entered on the first bar where confirmation is reached, held for $h$ bars without re-entry during active hold, reporting Avg bps/trade, Hit Rate, Sharpe, Sortino, n_trades, and n_days.

Top-Two Selection Rule

Exactly two specifications are retained from each subsection grid based on the primary ranking metric. These retained candidates are documented for downstream consolidation.

5. Baseline Signal Diagnostics (GC_30 Reference)

Mathematical Formulation

$$\mu_t^{(30)} = \frac{1}{30} \sum_{i=1}^{30} V_{t-i} \quad \Big(\texttt{shift(1).rolling(30, min\_periods=5).mean()}\Big)$$ $$\text{Raw}_t = \frac{V_t}{\mu_t^{(30)}}$$ $$L_t = \frac{1}{t-1} \sum_{s=1}^{t-1} |\text{Raw}_s| \quad \Big(\texttt{expanding(min\_periods=30).mean().shift(1)}\Big)$$ $$S_t = \frac{\text{Raw}_t}{L_t}$$

6. Section A — Baseline Construction

A.1 Lookback Length

1. Research Question

What is the effect on predictive IC of varying the trailing lookback window $k \in \{5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120\}$ bars used to calculate baseline volume?

2. Formula & Construction

$$\mu_t^{(k)} = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{i=1}^k V_{t-i}, \quad \text{Raw}_t^{(k)} = \frac{V_t}{\mu_t^{(k)}}, \quad S_t^{(k)} = \frac{\text{Raw}_t^{(k)}}{\text{expanding\_mean}(|\text{Raw}^{(k)}|)}$$

3. Test Setup

Lookback length $k$ is varied across $\{5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120\}$ bars across horizons $\{1, 5, 10, 30\}$ minutes. Expanding normalization, COMEX GC total volume, close window [15:00, 16:00), and GLD target returns remain fixed.

4. Retained Results

The two specifications with the highest signed Pearson IC from the 28-cell grid, alongside the baseline control:

Candidate Lookback ($k$) Horizon Pearson IC Spearman IC Avg bps Hit Rate Sharpe Sortino n_obs vs. Baseline IC
A1_lb90_h30 90 bars 30m +0.029585 +0.014699 +0.820251 50.05% 0.992215 1.674910 14,623 +0.012968
A1_lb120_h30 120 bars 30m +0.028562 +0.018539 +0.689140 50.05% 0.933104 1.534912 14,624 +0.011945

6. Interpretation

Observed Numerical Pattern
Across the tested lookback values at the 30-minute horizon, Pearson IC values were: 0.002113 (5b), 0.006889 (10b), 0.010805 (15b), 0.016617 (30b), 0.021547 (60b), 0.029585 (90b), and 0.028562 (120b). The 90-bar and 120-bar lookbacks produced the highest 30-minute Pearson IC values in the grid, exceeding the 30-bar baseline by +0.012968 and +0.011945 respectively. The 90-bar and 120-bar specifications at 30m are retained.

A.2 Expanding vs. Rolling Normalization

1. Research Question

What is the effect on predictive IC of replacing expanding normalization with rolling-window normalization over spans of 60, 390, or 1950 bars?

2. Formula & Construction

$$L_t^{(\text{roll}, W)} = \frac{1}{W} \sum_{i=1}^W |\text{Raw}_{t-i}| \quad \text{for } W \in \{60, 390, 1950\}, \quad S_t = \frac{\text{Raw}_t}{L_t}$$

3. Test Setup

Normalization window is varied across expanding, rolling-60, rolling-390, and rolling-1950. Lookback (30 bars), volume series (GC total), close window [15:00, 16:00), and GLD targets remain fixed.

4. Retained Results

Rolling-1950 produced a 30-minute Pearson IC of +0.017248 compared with +0.016617 for expanding normalization (+0.000631 difference). 7. Section B — Alternative Surge Definitions

B.1 Mean vs. Median Denominator

1. Research Question

What is the effect of replacing the 30-bar rolling mean volume denominator with the 30-bar rolling median volume denominator?

2. Formula & Construction

$$\text{Med}_t^{(30)} = \text{median}(V_{t-1}, \dots, V_{t-30}), \quad \text{Raw}_t^{\text{med}} = \frac{V_t}{\text{Med}_t^{(30)}}, \quad S_t^{\text{med}} = \frac{\text{Raw}_t^{\text{med}}}{\text{expanding\_mean}(|\text{Raw}^{\text{med}}|)}$$

3. Test Setup

Denominator varied (mean vs. median); lookback (30 bars), expanding normalization, GC volume, and close window fixed.

B.2 Percentile Rank Construction

1. Research Question

What is the effect of replacing the volume ratio with the percentile rank of current volume within the trailing 30 bars?

$$\text{Pct}_t^{(30)} = \frac{1}{30} \sum_{i=1}^{30} \mathbb{I}\big(V_t > V_{t-i}\big), \quad S_t^{\text{pct}} = \frac{\text{Pct}_t^{(30)}}{\text{expanding\_mean}(\text{Pct}^{(30)})}$$

3. Test Setup

Percentile rank tested across horizons; lookback (30 bars), GC volume, and close window fixed.

B.4 Total-Volume, Uptick-Volume, and Downtick-Volume Surges

1. Research Question

What is the predictive relationship of uptick-volume surge and downtick-volume surge compared with total-volume surge?

2. Formula & Construction

$$S_t^{\text{up}} = \frac{V_t^{\text{up}} / \text{mean}(V_{t-1}^{\text{up}}, \dots, V_{t-30}^{\text{up}})}{\text{expanding\_mean}(|\text{Raw}^{\text{up}}|)}, \quad S_t^{\text{down}} = \frac{V_t^{\text{down}} / \text{mean}(V_{t-1}^{\text{down}}, \dots, V_{t-30}^{\text{down}})}{\text{expanding\_mean}(|\text{Raw}^{\text{down}}|)}$$

Uptick-volume surge scales uptick volume against its own trailing uptick baseline. It is distinct from net volume differences or directional ratios.

3. Test Setup

The volume surge calculation is applied separately to total volume, uptick volume, and downtick volume; 30-bar lookback, expanding normalization, close window [15:00, 16:00), and GLD targets fixed.

6. Interpretation

Observed Numerical Pattern & Same-Burst Caveat
At the 1-minute horizon, uptick-volume surge produced a positive Pearson IC (+0.035301), downtick-volume surge produced a negative Pearson IC (−0.020735), and total-volume surge was −0.003982. At 30m, uptick-volume surge was +0.015666, downtick-volume surge was +0.010093, and total-volume surge was +0.016617.

Same-Burst Dependence: At a 1-minute horizon, adjacent elevated minutes can represent parts of the same underlying activity burst, meaning observations may not be independent. This requires burst-level de-duplication testing (e.g., one entry per burst) before the 1m result can be evaluated as an independent trading signal. Additionally, whether the 1m result is related to GC price movements leading GLD remains an untested question.

7. Decision / Retained Candidates

Retained: B4_uptick_h1 (provisional) and B4_uptick_h10.

B.5 Instrument Set Evaluation

1. Research Question

What is the predictive IC when volume surge is constructed on standard GC futures versus Micro Gold (MGC), an ounce-weighted composite ($100 \cdot V^{\text{GC}} + 10 \cdot V^{\text{MGC}}$), an unweighted equity ETF volume basket, or the GC/ETF volume ratio?

2. Formula & Construction

3. Test Setup

Volume source varied; 30-bar lookback, expanding normalization, close window [15:00, 16:00), and GLD targets fixed.

8. Section C — Surge Dynamics

C.1 Static Level vs. Velocity vs. Acceleration

1. Research Question

What is the predictive IC of continuous velocity $V_t^{(k)} = S_t - S_{t-k}$ and acceleration $A_t^{(k)} = S_t - 2S_{t-k} + S_{t-2k}$ over $k \in \{1, 5, 15\}$ minutes, compared with static surge level $S_t$?

2. Formula & Construction

$$V_t^{(k)} = S_t - S_{t-k}, \quad A_t^{(k)} = S_t - 2S_{t-k} + S_{t-2k}$$

3. Test Setup

Dynamic construction varied; baseline GC volume, 30-bar lookback, expanding norm, close window [15:00, 16:00) fixed.

4. Retained Results

Candidate Construction Horizon Pearson IC Spearman IC Avg bps Hit Rate Sharpe Sortino n_obs

C.2 Confirmation Duration & Persistence (Event Screen)

1. Research Question

What are the observed forward returns when entering only after a volume surge has remained above an expanding 80th percentile threshold for $N \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ consecutive bars?

2. Formula & Entry Rule

$$\text{Threshold}_t = \text{expanding(min\_periods=50).quantile(0.80).shift(1)}$$ $$E_t = \mathbb{I}\big(S_t > \text{Threshold}_t\big)$$

Entry triggers on the bar where the streak of consecutive elevated minutes first reaches $N$ bars ($N_t = N$). One entry per burst is permitted for that confirmation rule.

3. Test Setup

Evaluated on event-conditioned forward returns in basis points. Non-overlapping strategy holds for $h$ bars without re-entry during active hold.

C.3 Burst Evolution Phase Analysis

1. Research Question

What are the observed forward returns conditioned on the structural phase of an elevated surge?

2. Causal Phase Definitions

Conditioned on $S_t > \text{Threshold}_t$:

  • Onset: First minute of an elevated surge ($N_t = 1$).
  • Rising Flank: Elevated, streak $\ge 2$, and $S_t > S_{t-1}$.
  • Persistence: Elevated, streak $\ge 2$.
  • Confirmed Fade: Elevated, $S_t < S_{t-1}$, and $S_{t-1} > S_{t-2}$.

3. Test Setup

Evaluated on event-conditioned mean forward return in bps across horizons.

While unconditional continuous velocity in C.1 did not improve IC across the entire sample, conditioning on an elevated state in C.3 produced different observed returns across phases.

9. Section D — Time-of-Day Window Conditioning

1. Research Question

What is the predictive IC of the baseline signal when conditioned on sub-windows of the cash close?

2. Window Definitions

$$\text{Early Close: } 15:00 \le t < 15:30 \quad | \quad \text{Last Half-Hour: } 15:30 \le t < 16:00 \quad | \quad \text{Full Close: } 15:00 \le t < 16:00$$ $$\text{IC}_{(W, h)} = \text{Corr}\Big(S_t, R_{t, t+h}^{\text{GLD}} \;\Big|\; t \in W\Big)$$

3. Test Setup

The baseline signal $S_t$ is held fixed; only the conditioning timestamp window $W$ is varied.

4. Retained Results

Observed Numerical Pattern & Sample Size Consideration
In the 15:00–15:30 window, the 30-minute Pearson IC was +0.028412, compared with +0.001267 in the 15:30–16:00 window and +0.016617 across the full 15:00–16:00 window. The early-close sample ($n=7,328$) contains approximately half the observations of the full-close sample ($n=14,609$), meaning these values represent descriptive comparisons across different sample sizes rather than identical-sample controlled tests.

7. Decision / Retained Candidates

Retained: D_early_close_h30 and D_full_close_h30.

11. Completed-Scope Conclusion

Across the completed single-axis screens in Sections A through D, several distinct numerical patterns were observed. In Section A, longer reference lookbacks produced higher 30-minute Pearson IC values than the 30-bar baseline, with the 90-bar lookback producing 0.029585 and the 120-bar lookback producing 0.028562, compared with 0.016617 for the baseline. Alternative normalization methods produced smaller differences, with rolling-1950 producing 0.017248 and shorter rolling windows producing lower IC values.

In Section B, median denominator (0.017526) and percentile rank (0.017110) constructions produced 30-minute Pearson IC values close to the baseline ratio (0.016617), while the logarithmic transformation produced a lower value (0.012727). In Section B.4, uptick-volume surge produced a positive 1-minute Pearson IC of +0.035301, while downtick-volume surge was −0.020735 and total-volume surge was −0.003982; at 30m, uptick-volume surge (0.015666) was close to total-volume surge (0.016617). Standalone COMEX GC volume produced a higher 30-minute IC (0.016617) than MGC (0.014011) or composite constructions.

In Section C, continuous velocity and acceleration specifications produced Pearson IC values between −0.0166 and +0.0012, not improving on the static baseline. In event screens, conditioning on 4 consecutive bars above an expanding 80th percentile threshold produced an observed mean 30-minute return of +3.937 bps ($n=129$ events), and entering during the rising flank produced +1.760 bps ($n=569$) compared with +0.620 bps at onset ($n=1,994$). In Section D, the 30-minute Pearson IC in the 15:00–15:30 window was 0.028412 ($n=7,328$), compared with 0.001267 in the 15:30–16:00 window ($n=7,281$).

These are the results of the completed one-axis analyses through Section D. They should not be interpreted as a final combined or out-of-sample strategy result.
